01 / The essentials

Six rules. You’re in.

Learn these first, then let the rallies do the teaching.

01

Serve diagonally.

Start behind the baseline and serve into the opposite service box, beyond the kitchen line. You get one attempt. Start a serving turn from the right.

02

Keep the serve low.

For a volley serve, swing upward, contact below your waist, and keep the paddle head below your wrist. Or drop the ball naturally and hit it after it bounces.

03

Let it bounce. Twice.

The receiver lets the serve bounce. The serving team lets the return bounce. After those two bounces, you can volley or play off a bounce.

04

Respect the kitchen.

No volleys while touching the kitchen or its line. Your momentum cannot carry you in after a volley, either. Enter freely to play a ball that has bounced.

05

Keep the rally alive.

Return the ball over the net before it bounces twice. Hitting out, into the net, or breaking a rule loses the rally. Boundary lines are in; a serve on the kitchen line is out.

06

Serve to score.

In standard scoring, only the serving side earns points. Score a point, switch service sides, and serve again. Play to 11 and win by at least 2.

The rhythm of a rally

Bounce. Bounce. Game on.

01 → THE SERVE

Receiver lets it bounce.

The serve lands in the diagonal service box before the receiver returns it.

02 → THE RETURN

Server lets it bounce.

The serving side waits for the return to land before hitting the third shot.

03 → THE RALLY

Now you can volley.

Hit in the air or after a bounce. The kitchen restriction still applies.

02 / Keep the score

What does “4–2–1” mean?

In doubles, call three numbers before serving: your team’s score, their score, and which server you are.

4–2–1
YOUR SCORETHEIR SCORESERVER 1 OR 2

You have 4, they have 2, and you’re the first server of this serving turn.

The serving rotation, explained.

What happens when we lose a rally?

In doubles, server 1 passes the serve to their partner. After server 2 loses a rally, the other team serves—a “side out.” Each server keeps serving until a fault.

Why does a game start at 0–0–2?

The first team to serve gets only one server’s turn. Calling “0–0–2” makes their first fault a side out. After that, both partners get a turn.

How is singles different?

Call only your score and your opponent’s score. Serve from the right when your score is even, and the left when it is odd. Lose a rally on your serve and your opponent serves.

What if the serve clips the net?

Play continues if the serve clears the kitchen and its line and lands in the correct service box. There is no automatic replay for hitting the net.

Can I stand in the kitchen?

Yes—even before the ball bounces. The restriction is on volleying. After entering, establish both feet outside the kitchen before your next volley.

03 / Court check

Can you make this call?

You volley from outside the kitchen, but your momentum carries your foot onto the kitchen line. Legal shot?
